summary: Speakeasy is a dense Vital Lacerda worker-placement game where players run rival Prohibition-era speakeasies, juggling territory influence, production chains, and card-driven abilities across a tightly interlocked system. Like his other designs, it rewards long-term planning and punishes wasted actions, with a heavy rules load up front.
praised: deeply interlocking systems where every decision ripples elsewhere
strong thematic integration of Prohibition-era mob business
high replayability from Lacerda's typical density of options
criticised: steep rules teach and long playtime that can alienate casual players
prone to analysis paralysis given how many systems interact
niche appeal outside dedicated heavy-euro gamers

interaction.detail: Mobsters place workers and influence across the same set of Manhattan districts, competing for majority control and limited district actions. Taking a district or action spot can deny it to opponents, though there is no direct removal of opponents' pieces.

scoring.how_you_win: Build up your speakeasy operation by controlling districts, brewing and delivering product to fulfill contracts, and climbing the reputation track; the highest combined score when the game-end trigger fires wins.
